basic_details.short_information: The Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT) is inviting applications for 1 post (the notice does not print a number) of Head, Centre for WTO Studies (CWTOS). The post is on contract or deputation basis. IIFT is an autonomous body under the Department of Commerce & Industry, Government of India. Academicians, candidates from industry and officers on deputation may apply. They must send a CV by email, addressed to the Registrar, IIFT, New Delhi, at [email protected], latest by 9 November 2026.

content_sections.heading: About IIFT
content_sections.text: The Indian Institute of Foreign Trade is a Deemed to be University. It is an autonomous body under the Department of Commerce & Industry, Government of India. The notice describes it as a premier institution of education, training and research in International Business, set up by the Department of Commerce. The Department of Commerce set up the Centre for WTO Studies in 1999 as a professional body. The Centre provides research and allied inputs to the government for negotiations at the WTO and for other WTO mandated committees. It now works under the Centre for Research on International Trade (CRIT), which is part of IIFT.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Write the application addressed to the Registrar, IIFT, New Delhi. Make the application clearly state that it is the "application for the post of Head, Centre for WTO Studies". Attach your CV. Attach a brief one-page write-up explaining why you consider yourself suitable for this post. Applications received without the write-up shall be rejected. Government officers send the application through the proper channel, with the documents listed under Enclosures. Email the application to [email protected] latest by 9 November 2026. content_sections.heading: IIFT Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The Head of the Centre for WTO Studies is the Chief Executive of the Centre. The responsibilities include: Planning, implementing and monitoring the annual work programme of the Centre. Supervising the day-to-day functioning of the Centre, so that its objectives under Clause 4 of the Bye-laws of the Centre are met effectively. Undertaking research to help India's trade negotiators and policy makers take part effectively in the WTO and in related multilateral/bilateral trade negotiations. Improving stakeholders' understanding of key trade issues through outreach and dissemination activities. Helping to build consensus, and building capacity in India and other developing countries to analyse WTO and other trade-related issues through training programmes.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: All applicants send: CV A brief one-page write-up on why the candidate is suitable for this post Government officers also send these documents with their application, through the proper channel: Attested photocopies of the APARs/Confidential Reports for the last five years, authenticated by an officer not below the rank of Under Secretary to the Government of India Vigilance & Cadre Clearance No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the parent organisation

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection has two stages: shortlisting of applications, then an interview. Shortlisting: If there are a large number of applications, the scrutiny committee may apply benchmarks higher than the minimum essential/desirable qualifications to shortlist candidates for the interview. Interview: Shortlisted candidates must appear for an interview before the Selection Committee at New Delhi. Only shortlisted candidates will be told the date and time of the interview, by email, in due course. Travel: Outside candidates must arrange their own travel and stay. IIFT will not bear any expenditure on this account. Verification: Selection, appointment and employment depend on meeting the required qualification and experience. They also depend on verification of testimonials, antecedents and past service.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in IIFT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There is 1 vacancy, for the post of Head, Centre for WTO Studies (CWTOS), on contract or deputation basis. The notice does not print a number of vacancies.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the IIFT Head, Centre for WTO Studies post?
faq.answer: Applications must be emailed to [email protected] latest by 9 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification do academicians need for the IIFT Head, CWTOS post?
faq.answer: Ph.D. is essential. Academicians also need at least 55% (or an equivalent grade) at bachelor's and master's level, and at least 10 years of relevant experience. Eight of those years should be at the level of Assistant/Associate Professor.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the IIFT Head, Centre for WTO Studies post?
faq.answer: Candidates should be at least 40 years of age at the time of appointment.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of the Head, Centre for WTO Studies at IIFT?
faq.answer: The selected candidate will be placed in the Academic Pay Level-14. The notice says this is subject to revision.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for IIFT Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Email your CV and a one-page write-up on why you are suitable to [email protected], addressed to the Registrar, IIFT, New Delhi. The application must clearly say it is the "application for the post of Head, Centre for WTO Studies".

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for the IIFT Head, CWTOS post?
faq.answer: Applications are shortlisted, and the scrutiny committee may apply higher benchmarks if there are many applications. Shortlisted candidates are then interviewed by the Selection Committee at New Delhi, and they will get the date and time by email.

faq.question: Q8. Is the IIFT Head, Centre for WTO Studies post permanent?
faq.answer: No. The appointment is on contract or deputation basis, for three years with a one-year probation at first. The contract may be extended for up to three years, or for a period the Chairperson of CRIT decides. For a Government officer, the first deputation period is three years, extendable under DoPT instructions.

faq.answer: No. IIFT shall reject applications received without the one-page write-up.
